title: I've been using an AI voice for my game's host through development. Now I'm auditioning actors, and so far the AI is better
author: OkBank8023
selftext:
The host of my party quiz game has been an AI voice since September: a camp, sardonic British game-show host I designed in ElevenLabs, with delivery tags in every line and the best of a few takes picked by hand.

It was genuinely useful. Playtesters heard all 813 lines in context from the first week, and I rewrote much of the script because of it.

But I'd rather ship with a real actor. A lot of players don't want AI voices in games, and the host is the character people remember, so I don't want him to be the thing they object to. Since early November I've been auditioning with a paid 10-line script. Quotes ran from about $70 to \~$1,500, and at my budget nobody has quite found him yet.

What I'd like to know:

* If you've replaced a placeholder voice, how did you brief the actor so they didn't just imitate it?
* For about 850 lines, what rate and what budget for pick-ups is normal?
* Would you ship with the AI voice and say so, or wait for the actor?

comments.author: FPH_Gaming
comments.body: mind if I have a listen to the AI voice?

replies.author: FPH_Gaming
replies.body: That's actually really good. In my opinion, I wouldn't even bother disclosing it's an AI voice with all the negativity around using AI in game dev lately. Big companies get away with it and the only reason indie devs get punished more by the idiots on Reddit for it is because they're an easier target.

comments.author: Big_Presentation2786
comments.body:
Build the best game you can with or without AI..

If people are complaining, your gameplay isn't good enough..
That's all there is to it..

If COD4 and FIFA is allowed to use AI, so are indie devs

replies.author: OkBank8023
replies.body: yeah, I honestly thought that a voice actor would just be better... but honestly, I'm happy with AI, it's frighteningly good to be fair and now everyone I audition just doesn't cut it.

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
Honestly? 

This is more than likely due to yourself being inexperienced in development rather than voice actors lacking talent..

In an effort to get the most from a voice actor, you'd need to prepare a solid script, have interaction coaching, and express emotion through a physical scene they can visualise.

Asking someone to say something and act scared is quite a distance away from getting actors Infront of a game screen and showing them how the scene will play out, before taking multiple takes and replaying it Infront of a producer..

If you've genuinely got 1500 bucks to spend on a scene hire a sound producer to do the work for you.

Good audio will levitate your gameplay.

comments.author: ItsDumi
comments.body:
Don't send the actor the placeholder voice at all. Thus they won't imitate it. Find genuine references of voice performances you enjoy from animations or games. Write down the reasons why you like it as a references (gravitas, clarity, seriousness or quickness, sarcasm or what? Deep tone? High pitched? Nerdy?)

You need to see yourself as a director. a good actor can only do so much with a bad director. Also, ask them what they need. You'll learn way more from the horses mouth

replies.author: OkBank8023
replies.body:
\> Don't send the actor the placeholder voice at all.

yeah, I haven't done so... I've provided a character idea and notes about delivery in each line (almost the same as how I generated the AI lines, but so far, I'm just happier with the AI versions)

replies.author: spstks
replies.body: you are the director, probably treating your actors like ai agents. you need to read up on directing voice performances and search the fault in you, not in the humans

replies.author: OkBank8023
replies.body: so with the correct directing of the voice performance, all talent at all levels returns equal quality. got it

replies.author: zimmer550king
replies.body: Of course someone like Nathan Drake can perform better than an AI voice but I bet OP does not have the money to pay that much money. That’s why AI is much better for his budget

replies.author: spstks
replies.body: this will get upvoted but it will stay only true in this echochamber of people outside of reality

replies.author: OkBank8023
replies.body: before posting this reply had you researched the standard of the performances of people selling themselves as "voice actors" on some of the platforms? some are truly terrible

comments.author: LifeStartsToday
comments.body: can't help on vo rates, but on the last question: i shipped with ai art and just said so upfront, and most players who cared appreciated the honesty more than they minded the ai. if the actor isn't there yet, i'd ship and keep auditioning, then swap in an update. a voice that's this central is worth not rushing
